成化十七年進士登科錄

□□

□□七年二月十三日，禮部尚書臣周洪謨等於□□事，會試天下舉人，取中二百九十八名。本年□□日，□□□□讀卷官太子太保、吏部尚書□□學士萬安等五十二員。其進士出身等第，依皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六□□，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七□□，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。奉聖旨，欽此。

translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Seventeenth Year of Chenghua (1481)

[Two illegible characters]

On the thirteenth day of the second month of the [illegible] seventh year [?], your servant Zhou Hongmo, Minister of Rites, and others [illegible passage] conducted the Metropolitan Examination for provincial graduates from throughout the empire, selecting 298 successful candidates. On [illegible date] of the same year, [four illegible characters] the examination readers numbered fifty-two, including Wan An, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and [illegible designation] Academician [?]. The classes of their jinshi status followed the qualifications determined by the Emperor himself: the first class customarily comprised three men. The first-place candidate received lower sixth rank [illegible text], and the second- and third-place candidates received upper seventh rank; they were granted the designation “jinshi with honors.” The second class received lower seventh rank [illegible text] and the designation “regular jinshi.” The third class received upper eighth rank and the designation “associate jinshi.” The imperial command was received: “Respect this.”

[Illegible designation] Officials

Wan An held the prestige title of [illegible] Grand Master and served as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. 〔Jinshi of the wuchen year (1448).〕

Liu Xu held the prestige title of [illegible] Grand Master and served as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of [illegible ministry], and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Hall. 〔Jinshi of the wuchen year (1448).〕

Liu Ji held the prestige title of [illegible] Grand Master and served as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of [illegible ministry], and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Hall. 〔Jinshi of the wuchen year (1448).〕

translation_en:
Yin Min, Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel, was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuchen year.

Wang Yue, Earl of Weining and concurrently Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, held the titles of Civil Official Who Upholds Heaven, Assists in Protection, Displays Sincerity, Exerts Strength, and Maintains Rectitude; Specially Advanced Grand Master for Glorious Happiness; Pillar of State; and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Weng Shizi, Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Revenue, was a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.

Shi Chun, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Rites in charge of the Court of State Ceremonial, was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Chen Yue, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of War, was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Lin Cong, Grand Master for Fostering Virtue, Senior Minister for Correct Governance, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Justice, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year.

Liu Zhao, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Works, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

He Cong, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Transmission Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Song Min, Grand Master for Comprehensive Counsel, Governor for Aid in Governance, and Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Peng Hua, Grand Master for Comprehensive Counsel and Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Zhou Hongmo, Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Xu Pu, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Xie Yikui, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the gengchen year.

Examination Monitors:

Xu Jin, Gentleman for Service in the Literary Class and Investigating Censor for the Shandong Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Huang Jie, Gentleman for Service in the Literary Class and Investigating Censor for the Fujian Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Officials Receiving Examination Papers:

Jiao Fang, Expositor of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiashen year.

Lu Yue, Senior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiashen year.

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of Chenghua 17 (1481), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the seventeenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard arranged the imperial ceremonial equipage on the vermilion steps and in the vermilion courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites reverently carried the yellow results placard, led by drums and music, out beyond Chang'an Left Gate. Once the placard had been posted, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

translation_en:
On the eighteenth day of the third month, the Emperor bestowed a banquet at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the nineteenth day of the third month, the Emperor bestowed court robes, a cap, and a belt upon the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twentieth day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial of gratitude for imperial favor.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites memorialized the throne, requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names upon it.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the degree of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Wang Hua, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a Confucian scholar. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Dehui; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuzhun; his grandfather was Jie, a student of the Imperial University; his father was Tianxu; and his mother was née Cen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rong, and his younger brothers were Gun, Mian, Fu, and Fu. His wife was née Zheng. He ranked second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xun, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Tingxi; he was second in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zifang; his grandfather was Wen; his father was Lian, an Instructor at the Nanjing Imperial University; his mother was née Dai; and his stepmother was née Han. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chen, and his younger brothers were Zhen and Pei. His wife was née Zhu. He ranked first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tianrui, registered in Qingping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tianxiang; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Delu; his grandfather was Mingshan; his father was Hao; and his mother was née Han. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wang. He ranked third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second class: ninety-five graduates, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Hu Yu, courtesy name Bojian, was registered in an official household of the Taizhou Defense Battalion, Yangzhou Guard, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Kai, and his father Lun, a Company Commander; his mother was née Xue. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Lian, a Company Commander, Xuan, Zhen, and Gong. His wife was née Lu. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Wen, courtesy name Guandao, was registered in a military household in Gaoyao County, Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong. A National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maode, his grandfather Zuyin, and his father Zhishi; his mother was née Xie and his stepmother née Dong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tong and Biao. His first wife was née Tang, and his subsequent wife née Liang. He placed forty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Duanyi, courtesy name Kongshi, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Quan, an Assistant Instructor, and his father Ruqin, an Instructor; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qiao, Kan, Cheng, Jian, Qiu, Ru, and Zhuan. His wife was née Huang. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yuan 鄭瑗, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongbi; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yizhong; his grandfather, Dezai; and his father, Yihe, an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chen, and his wife was née Wang. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Jing 胡璟, registered in a civilian household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xisong; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shineng; his grandfather, Shiran; his father, Daning; and his mother, née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shan and Lian, and his younger brothers were Ying, Huan, and Gong. His wife was née Zhang. He placed 130th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Sicheng 東思誠, registered in a civilian household in Huazhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jindao; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lianghui, with an illegible annotation [□□]; his grandfather's name is illegible [□]. His father, Sheng, was a County Vice Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Bureau Director. His father's former wife was née Guo, and his mother, also née Guo, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Fengxian and Sizhong, the latter a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; his younger brother was Sigong, a tribute student (gongshi). His wife was née Guo. He placed sixteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Qi 楊奇, registered in a civilian household in Huguan County, Luzhou, Shanxi, was an additional student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiufu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyuan; his grandfather, Jie; and his father, Neng, a Prefectural Vice Prefect. His mother was née Niu, and his stepmother was née Zhao. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Sen, Qiao, and Fang, and his wife was née Wang. He placed eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Bingyi 陳秉彞, courtesy name Yichu, was from Shuyang County, Huai'an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was registered in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kang, Vice Magistrate of Jiangning County; his grandfather was Wan; his father was Duo; and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Bingjun, and his wife was née Zhong. He ranked forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Kuan 趙寬, courtesy name Lifu, was from Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was registered in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siming, an Unranked Clerk; his grandfather was Ying, a Bureau Commissioner; his father was Yang; and his mother was née Shen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Wan, and his younger brothers were Hong, Chong, and Cheng. His wife was née Mo. He ranked sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zan 張瓚, courtesy name Tingqi, was from Tangyin County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, and was registered in a military household. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twentieth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qizong; his grandfather was Rang; his father was Xing; his mother was née Chen; and his stepmother was née Jiao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Lian, and his wife was née Shan. He ranked forty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Jiao 孫交, courtesy name Zhitong, was from Anlu Subprefecture, Huguang, and was registered in an official household. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the eighteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Sheng; his father was Zhong; and his mother was née Qian. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shan (䄠) [?], Pang, Qiu, and Yi, and his wife was née Yang. He ranked sixty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Zongfu, courtesy name Kongxiu, was registered in a military household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuanhui; his grandfather, Youcheng, was an Assistant Instructor; and his father, Zhe, was an Instructor. His mother was née Cheng, and his stepmother née Fang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Zongru, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his younger brothers were Zongyu, Zongwu, Zongkui, and Zongnan. His wife was née Xiong. He ranked fifty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ou Rui, courtesy name Shijiao, was registered in a civilian household in Meizhou, Sichuan. A student of the department school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Junxiang; his grandfather was Bin; and his father, Lian, was an Investigating Censor. His legal mother was née Yang, and his birth mother née Wan. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zheng, a cultivated talent attached to the Hanlin Academy, and Yi, a Confucian scholar attached to the Ministry of Rites. His wife was née Wan. He ranked sixty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Ying, courtesy name Chaoying, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Chang; his grandfather was Yuan; his father was Shen; and his mother was née You. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Jun, Fang, and Wei. His wife was née Ju. He ranked eighty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Shen, courtesy name Tingpei, was registered in a civilian household in Qufu County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Fuyou; his grandfather was Gang; and his father, Feng, was an Assistant Teacher. His father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Kong. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shao, Chun, Lun, and Jin. His wife was née Kong. He ranked seventy-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

駱瓏〔貫浙江紹興府諸暨縣，民籍，縣學生，治禮記，字蘊良，行一，年三十二，十月初一日生〕。曾祖則民，祖公達，父章〔國子生〕，母丁氏。具慶下，弟琥、瓊，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第五十七名，會試第七十七名。

江潭〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字朝東，行一，年三十四，五月二十七日生〕。曾祖永寧，祖序瀾，父益明，母張氏。具慶下，弟漢、派、波，娶蔣氏。江西鄉試第七十八名，會試第二百八名。
translation_en:
Yuan Jie 原潔, courtesy name Bencheng, was registered in a civilian household in Zuocheng County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan; he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, fourth in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twentieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jichuan, his grandfather Guifang, his father Hai, and his mother née Zhao; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Huai, Ding, and Nai; he married a woman née Dong and subsequently a woman née Nie; he ranked sixty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shaoxuan 劉紹玄, courtesy name Xianzhi, was registered in a military household in Tongcheng County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang; he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, third in birth order, aged forty, and born on the seventeenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Mingde, his grandfather Yong, his father Chang, and his mother née Ding; his mother alone was living; his elder brothers were Shaowen and Shaozong; he married a woman née Huang; he ranked eleventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Long 駱瓏, courtesy name Yunliang, was registered in a civilian household in Zhuji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zemin, his grandfather Gongda, his father Zhang (a student of the Imperial University), and his mother née Ding; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Hu and Qiong; he married a woman née Chen; he ranked fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Tan 江潭, courtesy name Chaodong, was registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi; he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yongning, his grandfather Xulan, his father Yiming, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Han, Pai, and Bo; he married a woman née Jiang 蔣; he ranked seventy-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Xiangpeng, courtesy name Yuhan, was registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An additional student at the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked fifth in birth order, and was aged twenty-eight, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiuzhang; his grandfather, Zhongwu; his father, Dongzhen; and his mother, née Liu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Xiangqi (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Xiangfeng, Xianghuang, and Xiangjiao. He married a woman née Ren. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Lin, courtesy name Caimei, was registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Wenkuan; his father, Jie (an official awaiting selection for appointment); and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Lu. He married a woman née Ji. He placed thirty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xiao, courtesy name Zhixue, was registered in Nanling County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shanqing; his grandfather, Guangba; his father, Gui; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zi. He married a woman née Jin. He placed eighty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Sui, courtesy name Zhengchao, was registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. An additional student at the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-five, born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bochu; his grandfather, Yue (an assistant instructor); his father, Xuanqing (an instructor); his mother, née Kang; and his stepmother, née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Bai, and his younger brothers were Ci and Ju. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed eighty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yan Jiang, registered in a civilian household in Le'an County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chaozong; he was second in birth order, aged fifty-one, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Tianxi, his grandfather Wenhui, and his father □ [title illegible: □□]; his mother was née Yang and his stepmother née Ge. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tao, and his wife was née Song. He ranked thirty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dan, registered in a military household in Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a soldier of the Yulin Guard in Shaanxi who specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Qidong; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Sijing, his grandfather Wen, and his father Ji, a Daoist Instructor; his mother was née Wei. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ang, and his wife was née Chen. He ranked thirteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ji, registered in a civilian household in Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Kexiu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Fuxin, his grandfather Yi'an, and his father Shihao; his mother was née Shu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Wei held honorary official status, and his wife was née Gao. He ranked fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Siren, registered in a civilian household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shangde; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the sixteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Jingchun, and his father Ao, a County Vice Magistrate; his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Siwen and his younger brother Sixian. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Zhong. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

談詔〔貫直隸松江府上海縣，軍籍，縣學生，治春秋，字朝宣，行一，年三十一，十二月二十一日生〕。曾祖文政，祖悅，父甫〔縣丞〕，母宋氏。具慶下，弟誥，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第五名，會試第五十八名。
translation_en:
Hu Xuan, courtesy name Tingqi, was registered in Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked second among his brothers, and was born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month (no age is recorded). His great-grandfather was Zhongde, his grandfather Nan, his father Xi, and his mother née Zhang; his mother alone was still living, his elder brother was Huan, and his wife was née Feng; he placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lun, courtesy name Yongchang, was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qizhi, his grandfather Boxian, his father Duan, and his mother née Wu; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Yi 儀, Yi 億, Kan, Chou, and Si, and his wife was née Shi; he placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Fu, courtesy name Suizhi, was registered in Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household; he was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rixin, his grandfather Shimin, his father Shoufu, and his mother née Sheng; his father alone was still living, his elder brother was Dan, and his younger brothers were Shao and Ti 裼; his wife was née Zhu, and he subsequently married a woman née Shao; he placed twenty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Zhao, courtesy name Chaoxuan, was registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), in a military household; he was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzheng, his grandfather Yue, his father Fu〔County Vice Magistrate〕, and his mother née Song; both parents were living, his younger brother was Gao, and his wife was née Wang; he placed fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

尚縉〔貫河南睢陽衛，軍籍，浙江嘉興縣人，國子生，治禮記，字美儀，行二，年二十七，十一月二十六日生〕。曾祖雲，祖興，父福〔封員外郎〕，母趙氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄綱〔工部郎中〕，弟紳、紹、繻，娶劉氏。河南鄉試第七十名，會試第九十五名。

常麟〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉興縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字汝仁，行八，年二十七，四月初九日生〕。曾祖仲信，祖士昌〔知府〕，父縉，前母程氏，母馬氏。具慶下，兄鳳，弟龍，娶毛氏。浙江鄉試第五十三名，會試第二百十三名。
translation_en:
Gu Xiong, registered in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shijun. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizhan, a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather was Sishang, a County Vice Magistrate; and his father was De. His mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Fang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ni and Ke, and his wife was née Wu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Wei, registered in Cao County, Caozhou, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Minwang. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Tong, and his father Quan. His mother was née Jin and his stepmother née Bai. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yan, and his wife was née Lü. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shang Jin, registered in a military household of Suiyang Guard, Henan, was originally from Jiaxing County, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Meiyi. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun, his grandfather Xing, and his father Fu, who had been granted the honorary title of Vice Director. His mother, née Zhao, had been granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gang, a Director in the Ministry of Works; his younger brothers were Shen, Shao, and Xu. His wife was née Liu. He placed seventieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Lin, registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an added student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruren. He ranked eighth among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxin, his grandfather Shichang, a Prefect, and his father Jin. His father's former wife was née Cheng, and his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Feng and his younger brother Long; his wife was née Mao. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Kuan, courtesy name Lifu, was registered in a military household at Haining Battalion, Zhejiang, and was a native of Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture. A student of the Haining County school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-first day of the intercalary seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Cong; his father, Yi; and his mother, née Wang. His father was living, and his mother had died. His elder brother was Gong, and his younger brothers were Xin, Min, Hui, Xiao, You, and Mu. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed thirteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Zhe, courtesy name Tonggui, was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Junfu; his grandfather, Youxin; his father, Hai; and his mother, née Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Lu. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently women née Liu, Lei, Wang, and Ren. He placed thirteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Yan, courtesy name Tingxin, was registered in a military household in Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the fifteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Boqing; his grandfather, Chun, posthumously appointed Vice Director; and his father, Quan, Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Right in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Li, was granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother was née Bai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gui, an honorary official (yiguan); Zan; Cong; and Xi, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ai Pu, courtesy name Derun, was registered in a military household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Songs, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhiwen; his grandfather, Ye, a medical official with the title Director (zhengke); and his father, Cunren. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Hu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Bi. He married a woman née Wei. He placed fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Ji, courtesy name Ruzhou, was registered in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chongli, his grandfather Xixian, his father Li, and his mother Lady Shi. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Guan, and he married Lady Li. He ranked nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Cheng, courtesy name Wanli, was registered in Ouning County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyue, his grandfather Yanzhen, and his father You, a Professor; his father's former wife was Lady Chen, and his mother was Lady Zou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jun and Jie, and his younger brothers Mu and Ji. He married Lady Zhu and subsequently Lady Wu. He ranked seventy-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang You, courtesy name Jingzhi, was registered in Chun'an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Benzong, an honorary official, his father Zhiji, and his mother Lady Fang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Bin was a Prefect; his younger brothers were Chen, Bi, and Wan. He married Lady Xu. He ranked forty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Xian, courtesy name Shizhang, was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bai, his grandfather Yong, his father □ [name illegible], a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), and his mother Lady Zhou. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were You and Shi, and he married Lady Hua. He ranked eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Rao Si, registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhengyi. Second in birth order, he was aged forty-seven and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qiming, his grandfather Chongben, and his father Mengying, an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wife was née Zhu, and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zhu, and his younger brothers were He, Luo, and Zhan. His wife was née Yuan. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Fu, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanyue. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunzhong, his grandfather Shirui, his father Bangyan, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yan, Shen, Yong, Shuo, and Hao. His wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Di, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yunji. First in birth order, he was aged forty-two and was born on the fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bohe, his grandfather Bin, and his father Ci. His mother was née Zhao, and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhou and Jin. His wife was née Xiong. He placed fiftieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhou, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenmei. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Gongning, and his father Yu, a Vice Prefect. His mother was née Gu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Xuan. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Gui, courtesy name Weishan, was registered in a military household in Fucheng County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the fourteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongwen; his grandfather, Cheng; and his father, Liang, a Subprefect. His legal mother was née Zhou, and his birth mother was née Wang. His parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Lin, Yu, and Zhen, and his wife was née Gao. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qi, courtesy name Derun, was registered in a civilian household in Suichang County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fifth in birth order, aged forty-seven, and born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Lizhi; his grandfather, Dezheng; and his father, Siwu. His father's former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Yang. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Men, Yun, Yan, and Ke, and his wife was née Su. He placed eighty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Long, courtesy name Rulin, was registered in a civilian household in Yangwu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Ying; his father, Hai; and his mother, née Yang. His parents were deceased. His younger brother was Feng, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Huang, courtesy name Shijian, was registered in a civilian household in Huai'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuangui; his grandfather, Shun, who had been granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father, Jing, a Subprefect; and his mother, née Zhang, who had been granted the title of Lady (ruren). His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Lin (鏻), and his wife was née Zhou. He placed seventy-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張瀠〔貫雲南越州衛官籍，直隸含山縣人，曲靖軍民府學生，治書經，字宗周，行六，年三十四，九月初七日生〕。曾祖亨〔指揮僉事〕，祖昱〔正千戶〕，父敬〔指揮僉事〕，前母王氏，母蘇氏。慈侍下，兄淳〔指揮僉事〕、漢、溥、浩、演，弟湧，娶朱氏。雲南鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百六十二名。

孫霖〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字希說，行三，年三十七，三月十八日生〕。曾祖貴一，祖道祥，父俊，母徐氏。永感下，兄浩、澄，娶金氏，繼娶何氏。應天府鄉試第一百五名，會試第一百九十一名。
translation_en:
Zhou Feng, courtesy name Mingqi, was registered in an official household of Xi’an Front Guard in Shaanxi and was a native of Jiangdu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Chang’an County school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was sixth in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Degui, his grandfather Yu, and his father Tong; his father’s former wife was née Tian, and his mother was née Wei. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tang, Vice Commander; Zhen; Zhe; Cheng; and Qian; his younger brother was E. He was betrothed to a woman née Chen. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Liangfu, courtesy name Xizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Yishan County, Qingyuan Prefecture, Guangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fifteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Siyi; his grandfather, Yongjing, had been granted the title of Vice Director; his father, Jun, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Wu, had been granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Liangbi, Liangchen (an official of the School of Yin-Yang Studies), Liangzai, Liangmo, and Liangji. He married a woman née Tang. He placed fourteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ying, courtesy name Zongzhou, was registered in an official household of Yuezhou Guard in Yunnan and was a native of Hanshan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Qujing Military and Civil Prefecture school specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Heng, was an Assistant Commander; his grandfather, Yu, was a Battalion Commander; and his father, Jing, was an Assistant Commander. His father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Su. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Chun, Assistant Commander; Han; Pu; Hao; and Yan; his younger brother was Yong. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed thirty-second in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Lin, courtesy name Xishuo, was registered in a military household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the eighteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Guiyi, his grandfather Daoxiang, his father Jun, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hao and Cheng. He married a woman née Jin and subsequently a woman née He. He placed 105th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Zan, courtesy name Zongqi, was registered in a military household in Tongwei County, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiaoyi; his grandfather, Yi; his father, Sigong, an honorary official; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother Yu was a Medical Instructor. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twelfth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zhonghui, courtesy name Shouzhong, was registered in a military household in Wenxi County, Jiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan; his grandfather, Jian; his father, Bi, an Instructor; and his mother, née Yang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Zhongguang, and his younger brother was Zhongyao. He married a woman née Song. He placed tenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Mian, courtesy name Gongchen, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the fourteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen; his grandfather, Xin; his father, Xin; and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sheng, Ang, and Bing. He married a woman née Xi and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Zhou. He placed eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Che Ting, courtesy name Zhenqing, was registered in a civilian household in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Boliang and grandfather Xuan were both Astrologers; his father, Kezhao, was an honorary official; and his mother was née Zhao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother Lei was an Astrologer, and his younger brother Wen held the rank of Court Gentleman for Attendant Service. He married a woman née Yang. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Lin, registered in a military household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingpei, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged forty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Fuci, his grandfather Yilu, and his father Jingming, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under provisions of imperial grace; his father's principal wife was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Xu. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Qiong, Jin (a County Registrar), Xuan (a Station Master), and Yu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Xuan, registered in a salt-producing household in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tinghui, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the ninth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yuanli, his grandfather Mengwen, and his father Jingxian; his father's former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Jiang. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Cheng, Xuan, and Lian, his younger brothers were Qi and Zhang, and his wife was née He. He placed sixty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xu, registered in a civilian household in Shan County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shimian, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the twentieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zizhong, his grandfather Ying, and his father Xun; his father's former wife was née Xue, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Ang (an official awaiting selection for appointment), and his wife was née Shan. He placed forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Gui, registered in a civilian household in Wuyi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tianjue, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wengang, his grandfather Shi'an, and his father Xin; his father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Yu and Bi, and his wife was née Hong. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖德華 祖思顯〔贈監察 御史〕 父諒〔訓導〕 母俞氏 繼母章氏
具慶下 弟忱 娶徐氏

punctuated:
章啓〔貫武功中衛軍匠籍，直隸丹徒縣人，國子生，治易經，字際亨，行一，年三十，正月二十三日生〕。曾祖彥文，祖宣，父全，母蔣氏。重慶下，弟敏、敞、敦，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第五十四名，會試第二百六名。

宋旭〔貫浙江寧波府奉化縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字景暘，行一，年五十三，三月十三日生〕。曾祖信禮，祖原用〔教諭〕，父吉祥，母汪氏。永感下，弟暄〔教諭〕、昺〔訓導〕、旻〔國子生〕、暉、曇，娶毛氏。浙江鄉試第五十七名，會試第二十名。

孫旵〔貫直隸鎮江府金壇縣民籍，儒士，治書經，字愛暉，行二，年三十四，五月初二日生〕。曾祖禮，祖志堅，父謙，母徐氏，繼母鄧氏。具慶下，兄昻〔國子生〕，弟冕、暠、昪、暲，娶武氏。應天府鄉試第三十九名，會試第一百八十二名。

婁性〔貫江西廣信府上饒縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字原善，行一，年三十六，五月十五日生〕。曾祖德華，祖思顯〔贈監察御史〕，父諒〔訓導〕，母俞氏，繼母章氏。具慶下，弟忱，娶徐氏。江西鄉試第八十名，會試第一百五十九名。
translation_en:
Zhang Qi 章啓, courtesy name Jiheng, was registered in a military artisan household of Wugong Central Guard and was a native of Dantu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanwen, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Quan; his mother was née Jiang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Min, Chang, and Dun, and his wife was née Liu. He ranked fifty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Xu 宋旭, courtesy name Jingyang, was registered in a civilian household in Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged fifty-three, and born on the thirteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xinli, his grandfather Yuanyong, an Instructor, and his father Jixiang; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xuan, an Instructor; Bing, an Assistant Instructor; Min, a student of the Imperial University; Hui; and Tan. His wife was née Mao. He ranked fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Chan 孫旵, courtesy name Aihui, was registered in a civilian household in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Zhijian, and his father Qian; his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother née Deng. Both parents were living. His elder brother Ang was a student of the Imperial University; his younger brothers were Mian, Gao, Bian, and Zhang. His wife was née Wu. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lou Xing 婁性, courtesy name Yuanshan, was registered in a civilian household in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dehua, his grandfather Sixian, posthumously appointed an Investigating Censor, and his father Liang, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Yu, and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chen, and his wife was née Xu. He ranked eightieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xia Ying, registered in Dehua County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yucai. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shengbin, his grandfather Yizhang, and his father Mengde; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Hua and Xuan, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang You, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the prefectural Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shikuan. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Benran, his grandfather Jing, and his father Xiao; his mother was née Lin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His wife was née Chen. He placed fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jue, registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tingzhong. He ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Renyi, his grandfather Xian, and his father Zhining; his father's former wives were née Shi and née Yin, and his mother was née Duan. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Fu, a Director of a county Confucian school, Song, and Qi; his younger brothers were Fen, Lian, and Shu. His wife was née Yue. He placed thirtieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Jixue, registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Weizhi. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Chaoju, his grandfather Shulin, and his father Yingchao; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Shixue, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Hun, registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Boquan, he was second in birth order, and he was aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keding; his grandfather, Kuan; his father, Chao, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née He, and his stepmother née Liu. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Shen, and his younger brothers were Tan and Pu; his wife was née Dai. He placed seventy-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü He, registered in Dazhu County, Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shizhong, he was first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Caigui; his grandfather, Bin; his father, Xidao; and his mother, née Ren. Both parents were living. His wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Fu, registered in the Yiyong Front Guard in a military household and a native of Miyun County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenhua, he was fourth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hanchen; his grandfather, Ju; his father, Tong; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kuan, Ning, and Rong, and his younger brother was Xian; his wife was née Han. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yue, registered in Chenzhou, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shangchen, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renhai; his grandfather, Yijian, was a Vice Prefect posthumously granted the title of Secretary; his father, Jun, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his mother, née Liao, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren), and his stepmother, née Li, was granted the same title. His father and stepmother were living. His younger brother was Yan; his wife was née Li. He placed first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fang Xiang, courtesy name Yuyi, was from Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a military household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fa, a Judge; his grandfather was Mao, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Yu, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xi and Zhou, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Quan, courtesy name Wenheng, was from Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director; his grandfather was Xin, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel; his father was Bin, his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Zhen and Xi, and his wife was née Wu. He ranked sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Yan, courtesy name Guozhan, was from Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shizhe, his grandfather was Qianheng, his father was Wenxian, and his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Pai (㵺), and his younger brothers were He, Zhen, Kui (a tribute scholar), Yuan, and Ji; his wife was née Zhang. He ranked fiftieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Yuan, courtesy name Fengyuan, was from Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Youwen, his grandfather was Qian, and his father was Yu, a Prefectural School Instructor; his father's former wife was née Ding, and his mother was née Yin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ying and Cheng. His wife was née Shen, and his subsequent wife was née Liu. He ranked one hundred twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shao Cheng 邵誠, registered in a military household in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuankan; he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yangshi, his grandfather Jinsheng, his father Nengzheng, and his mother née Ying. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Nuo, and he married a woman née Li. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xian 陳憲, registered in a military household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Mengzhang; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zishou, his grandfather Shande, his father Tong, and his mother née Wang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Ying and Guang, and he married a woman née Lin. He placed eleventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yi 陳義, registered in a military household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yaoyi; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiande, his grandfather Cheng, his father Kui, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Diao and his younger brother Shan; he married a woman née Li. He placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xuan 陳宣, registered in a civilian household in Pingyang County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wende; he was second in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuyi, his grandfather Dan, his father Xu, his mother née Fang, and his stepmother née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Wendao, an honorary official for charitable contributions; his younger brothers were Jin and Bao. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed seventy-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Kang Shaozong, courtesy name Xiaolong, was registered in a military household of Yongqing Right Guard and was a native of Wuding Subprefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shixian; his grandfather, Rong; and his father, Xuan. His father's former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Xianzong, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked eighty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yong, courtesy name Ruxiu, was registered in a civilian household in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shangbin; his grandfather, Yanjun, was Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions in the Ministry of War [?—the bureau normally belonged to the Ministry of Rites]; and his father, Kongzhao, was a Director in the Ministry of Personnel. His mother, née Cai, had been granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Fu, and his wife was née Bao. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Tiyuan, courtesy name Yiqian, was registered in an artisan household in Qin Subprefecture, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jun, an Investigating Censor; his grandfather, Pu; and his father, Qiying. His mother was née Yan, and his stepmother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Tizhen, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Ding, courtesy name Tingqi, was registered in a military household in Heshui County, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Chen; his grandfather, Min; and his father, Jie. His mother was née Lin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Nai, Kui, Ting (䵺), and Zi, and his wife was née Tian. He ranked thirty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

沈庠〔貫應天府上元縣匠籍，直隸吳江縣人，國子生，治詩經，字尚倫，行一，年四十二，八月初二日生〕。曾祖伯義，祖仕澄，父安，母童氏。具慶下，娶韓氏，繼娶羅氏。順天府鄉試第二十四名，會試第一百六十七名。

胡宗道〔貫陝西鳳翔府扶風縣軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字守正，行一，年二十八，十一月初九日生〕。曾祖亨，祖全〔贈光祿寺署正〕，父恭〔光祿寺丞〕，母李氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，弟宗儒、宗顏、宗閔，娶杜氏。陝西鄉試第五名，會試第二百七十八名。
translation_en:
Yu Hong, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chongfan; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kejia, his grandfather Wenchang, his father Xuchu, and his mother née Wan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lie and Xiang, and his wife was née Hu. He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yanhua was registered in a military household of the Nanjing Rear Guard of the Reserved Garrison and was a native of Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Ruhe, was second in birth order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xingchuan, his grandfather Mengcheng, his father Wen, his mother née Zhou, and his successive stepmothers née Li and née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tong and his younger brother Zheng. He married a woman née Dong, then successively women née Jiang and née Zhou. He placed 129th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Xiang was registered in an artisan household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Wujiang County in the directly administered region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Shanglun, was first in birth order, and was aged forty-two, born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boyi, his grandfather Shicheng, his father An, and his mother née Tong. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Han and subsequently a woman née Luo. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Zongdao, registered in a military household in Fufeng County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shouzheng; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather Quan was posthumously granted the title of Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his father Gong was Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and his mother, née Li, was invested with the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zongru, Zongyan, and Zongmin, and his wife was née Du. He placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

侯直〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣民籍，府學生，治書經，字公繩，行六，年二十六，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖克紹，祖廷信，父藎〔運司同知〕，母沈氏〔封安人〕。嚴侍下，兄正、方〔刑部員外郎〕、洪、平、表，弟賢，娶林氏。應天府鄉試第七十六名，會試第七十名。

translation_en:
Zhang Kai, registered in a military household in Pinggu County, Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tingyi, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Daoming, his grandfather Bi, and his father Yun, a prefect; his mother was née Han, and his mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Ming, an honorary official, Zhu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Rui; his younger brothers were Xi, Yi, and Zheng; his wife was née Zhu. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chang, registered in a military artisan household of the Nanjing Embroidered-Uniform Guard, was a student of the Yingtian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Hanying, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Guoxiang, his grandfather Ning, and his father Zhong; his father's former wife was née Yuan, and his mother was née Zhang, with his mother alone still living. His elder brother was Zheng, his younger brother Gan, and his wife née Tian. He placed 106th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Zhi, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Gongsheng, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Keshao, his grandfather Tingxin, and his father Jin, an associate salt distribution commissioner; his mother was née Shen, granted the title Lady of Peace, and his father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Zheng, Fang, a vice director in the Ministry of Justice, Hong, Ping, and Biao; his younger brother was Xian, and his wife née Lin. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Rui Ji, registered in a civilian household in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weixin, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was thirty-six years old, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shuyuan, his grandfather Gongming, and his father Yiduan, granted the title of supervising secretary; his mother was née Zhang, granted the title Lady, and his mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Ji, a supervising secretary, Tian, and Wan; his wife was née Lu. He placed ninety-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.
