Third Class: 200 men, granted the status of equivalent metropolitan graduates (tong jinshi chushen).

Zhang Yingkui, a National University student registered in a civilian household in Putai County, Binzhou Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shizhen; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Boshou; his grandfather, Su, was a District Magistrate; his father, Zan, was a Prefectural Examiner; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingfu, Yingde, and Yingsu, the last a School Instructor. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Liangqi, a National University student registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yancheng; he was seventh in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Wenju, was a School Director under the Yuan dynasty; his grandfather, Yin, was a School Instructor posthumously awarded the title of District Magistrate; and his father, Minzheng, was a Prefect. His father's former wife, née Zheng, was posthumously awarded the title of ruren; his mother, née Zhang, was invested with the title of ruren. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Lianghan, Liangshi, Liangxin, Liangyu, Liangneng, and Liangmu. He married a woman née Dai. He placed ninetieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yan, a National University student registered in a military household in Fushan County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Tingshang; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhixiao; his grandfather, Yanbin, was posthumously awarded the title of Prefect; his father, Yu, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Fang, was invested with the title of gongren. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Ke, formerly an Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; Gui, a Supervising Secretary; and Zan, a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yao Long, from Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Fuheng. Third in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ren, a department magistrate; his grandfather was Koumin [?]; and his father was Kehou. His mother was Lady Xiao, and his stepmothers were Lady Xie and Lady Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Pu and Wu, and he married Lady Ai. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Fu, from Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Rubian. Second in birth order, he was forty-seven years old and was born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyi, his grandfather was Zhi, and his father was Fu (復). His mother was Lady Xia. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Fu (黼), and he married Lady Zhang. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Jian, from Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Gongjian. First in birth order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congrang, his grandfather was Yu, and his father was Yi, a district magistrate. His father's former wife was Lady Chen, and his mother was Lady Deng. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married Lady Ji. He placed forty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Rang, from Guang'an Department, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yunqian. First in birth order, he was thirty-nine years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Juren, his grandfather was Fushou, and his father was Hanliang. His mother was Lady Lin, and his stepmother was Lady Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mo and Cheng, and he married Lady Yang. He placed seventeenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Rui 許銳, courtesy name Jijie, was registered in a military household of Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang; a student of the Dengzhou Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuai, his grandfather Keming, his father Zhen (Gentleman for Rendering Service), and his mother née Liang; his mother alone was still living; his elder brothers were Jian (an honorary official recognized for charitable service), Yong, Qin, and Yue; he married a woman née Yan and placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Ting 謝烶, courtesy name Tingxian, was registered in a civilian household of Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zizhou (a Prefectural Clerk), his grandfather Xian, his father Yonghe, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Wang; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Guang and Shen; he married a woman née Li and placed 127th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Wenxu 郭文旭, courtesy name Zhongsheng, was registered in a military household of Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian; a Confucian scholar specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was seventh in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Lan (a Department Vice Magistrate), his father Jing, and his mother née Lin; his mother alone was still living; his elder brothers were Ye, Ang (an Assistant Instructor), Sheng, Yun, Gui, and Ding; he married a woman née Zheng and placed eighty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Qi 馮玘, courtesy name Liangyu, was registered in a military household of Huaiyuan Guard at Zhongdu and was a native of Changshu County in the directly administered metropolitan region; a student of the Fengyang County School specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Da, his father Shun, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living; his elder brother was Cong and his younger brother Lian; he married a woman née Li and placed sixty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Yi, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Julu; he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather was Tingqing, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his father was Qi, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother was née Zhang, ennobled as Lady (ruren). His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were You, Yong, Pan, Bi, and Ying; his younger brothers were Cang, Bo, Cheng, and Yi. He married a woman née Xu. He ranked fourteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Fu, registered in an artisan household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingbi; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sizhong, his grandfather Shugong, his father Yuandao, and his mother née Yu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yi and Zhen; his younger brothers were Jin, Kui, Yan, Bi, Zeng, and Zhong. He married a woman née Fu. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yin, registered in a civilian household in Rongcheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the eleventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Neng, his father Zhiguang, and his mother née Hu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Xian, Chen, and You. He married a woman née Li. He ranked 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qi, registered in a military household in Cangwu County, Wuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Tingxin; he was third in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziming, his grandfather Wencong, and his father Biao, a Prefectural Vice Prefect. His mother was née Ni and his stepmother née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Lin, an Assistant Instructor, and Luan, an Assistant Prefect; his younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Yan. He ranked fourth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He ranked fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Liang, registered in a salt-producing household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mingyu; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Mingyuan, his grandfather Shuxiang, his father Gong, and his mother née Bao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ying and Xiong, his younger brother was Xian, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Jingwu; he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twentieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yongtai, his grandfather Xian (a district magistrate), his father Congshan, his mother née Zhou, and his stepmother née Lu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qing and Hao, and his wife was née Wu. He ranked ninety-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Biao, registered in a commoner household in Xiping County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dazhang; he was second in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the eighteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Qing, his father Yuan, and his mother née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Jucai, and his wife was née Guo. He ranked twenty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang En, registered in a medical household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Tianchong; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhongwei, his grandfather Lian, and his father Xun; his mother was née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His wife was née Lu. He ranked seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Cheng, registered in a civilian household in Xihua County, Chenzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tianying; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Di, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Ming, a Medical Instructor. His father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Niu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yuan, and his younger brothers were Qing and Shen. His wife was née Liu. He ranked forty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Fengming, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yingwen; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Peng, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Fu, granted the honorary title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Qi, a Provincial Surveillance Commissioner. His mother, née Li, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fengyi, and his younger brother was Fengxiang. His wife was née Wang. He ranked second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Fu, registered in a military household of the Xi'an Front Guard, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Defu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Mengyi; his grandfather was Ying, posthumously granted the title of Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and his father was Duo, a Subprefect. His mother, née Zhao, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qi, and his younger brother was You. His wife was née Wu. He ranked thirtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Dan, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Yun; his father was Ping; and his mother was née Zeng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His courtesy name was Shangzhi; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather was Zheng; his father was Yanming; his mother was née Xiao; and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wu and Yun, and his wife was née Pang. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yiguan, registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daofu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cifu; his grandfather was Yangsheng, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under provisions for imperial grace; his father was Tingji; his mother was née Tang; and his stepmother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zan, Zi, and Zhi, and his wife was née Huang. He ranked fifteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Chengxue, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. 歐陽旦〔貫江西吉安府安福縣軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字子相，行一，年三十三，十一月十三日生〕。曾祖友倫，祖伯璇，父𨗳，母王氏。具慶下，弟晢〔貢士〕、魯，娶周氏。江西鄉試第四名，會試第五名。

王瑫〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣民籍，儒士，治易經，字宗玉，行四，年二十六，正月二十四日生〕。曾祖伯智，祖惟德，父輩謙，母張氏。具慶下，兄璦、瑭、斑，弟璐、玢、瓊、琳，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第四十名，會試第九十八名。
translation_en:
Wang Ding’an 王定安, courtesy name Zhishan, was registered in the wealthy-household category in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Huai’an County, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weiyi, his grandfather Xuan, his father Fu, and his mother née Gao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Dingning, and his wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qi 李𤪌, courtesy name Demei, was entered in the official register of the Chief Military Commission of the Right and was a native of Xining Guard, Shaanxi. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Nanqi, granted the title Earl of Huining; his grandfather was Ying, Earl of Huining; his father was Gao, Assistant Commissioner-in-chief; and his mother was née Hu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Qi 玘, an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Shan, Yu, Fan, Yu [?—the name occurs twice], Cheng, Qi 琦, Lin, and Pei. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed one hundred thirtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Dan 歐陽旦, courtesy name Zixiang, was registered in the military-household category in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youlun, his grandfather Boxuan, his father Dao 𨗳, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhe, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Lu; his wife was née Zhou. He placed fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tao 王瑫, courtesy name Zongyu, was registered in the civilian-household category in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bozhi, his grandfather Weide, his father Beiqian 輩謙 [?], and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ai, Tang, and Ban; his younger brothers were Lu, Bin, Qiong, and Lin. His wife was née Chen. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Shouyue, registered in a military household in Henei County, Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xizeng; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the eleventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Fu, Deputy Battalion Commander; his grandfather was Dong; his father was Jian; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shoudao and Shoujing, and his wife was née Dong. He ranked thirty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Bingran, registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Sijin; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the eleventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Fu, Magistrate; his grandfather was Weiqing, posthumously granted the title of Secretary; his father was Qin, Prefect; and his mother was née Wang, granted the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhanran and his younger brother was Jiongran; his wife was née Ran. He ranked eleventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhen, registered in a military household in Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guoxing; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shaoxian; his grandfather was Qin; his father was Lin; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xiang, and his wife was née He. He ranked twenty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Rui, registered in a civilian household in Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Tingyue; he was second in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shou; his grandfather was Heng; his father was Gang, Postal Station Master; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother’s name is illegible (□); his younger brothers were Hai and Qian. His wife was née Zhao, and he subsequently married a woman née Wang. He ranked seventy-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Zhen, of a civilian household registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shiqi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongliang, his grandfather Shide, his father Shuren, and his mother née Xie; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Ze, Hui 撝, Zhuan, Yuan, and Jian 揀, and his wife was née Xue; he placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Xun, of a civilian household registered in Feixiang County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shigong, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanshen, his grandfather Xiang, a Guard Registrar, his father Feng, a County Magistrate, and his mother née Yan; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Yong and Long, and his wife was née Zhu; he placed ninety-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Wen, of a civilian household registered in Queshan County, Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zaidao, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Hao, his father Qi, Commissioner of a Tax Office, and his mother née Tian; both parents were living, and he was betrothed to a woman née Huang; he placed fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Ming, of a civilian household registered in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dingfu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the eleventh day of the intercalary fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, a Prefect, his grandfather Guan, his father Zuo, and his mother née Qu; his father was deceased and his mother living, his younger brother was Li 曆, and he married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Yang; he placed third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫治〔貫江西臨江府清江縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字五美，行二，年四十九，閏八月初一日生〕。曾祖思誠〔稅課司大使〕，祖執輿，父永常，母吳氏。永感下，兄五典，娶彭氏。江西鄉試第二十七名，會試第一百二十九名。

胡昂〔貫直隸保定府定興縣，官籍，國子生，治書經，字文謙，行二，年二十六，十月二十八日生〕。曾祖林〔百戶〕，祖本〔百戶〕，父𤣾〔百戶〕，母李氏。具慶下，兄昱，弟昪、晟、杲、昷、景，娶陳氏。順天府鄉試第十五名，會試第二百五十五名。
translation_en:
Chen Chongde, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jiguang. Second in birth order, he was thirty-six years old and was born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai; his grandfather, Gong, was an Assistant Instructor; and his father was Xu. His father's former wife and his mother were both née Lin. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Shunde, and his wife was née Pan. He ranked forty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Duan, registered in Zaoyang County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Biaozheng. First in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Zhong, his father He, and his mother née Gao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers are listed as Jing, Hong, Yi, Gui, Shen, Fei, Xian, Xuan, Zhuan, and Qiang [the transcription of the names from Gui onward is doubtful: 媯妽妃嫌嫙嫥嬙, ?]. His wife was née Ren. He ranked eighteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Zhi, registered in Qingjiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Wumei. Second in birth order, he was forty-nine years old and was born on the first day of the intercalary eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Sicheng, was Commissioner of a Tax Office; his grandfather was Zhiyu, his father Yongchang, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Wudian, and his wife was née Peng. He ranked twenty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Ang, registered in Dingxing County, Baoding Prefecture, the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Wenqian. Second in birth order, he was twenty-six years old and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Lin, grandfather Ben, and father 𤣾 [reading uncertain, ?] were all Company Commanders. His mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yu, and his younger brothers were Bian, Sheng, Gao, Wen, and Jing. His wife was née Chen. He ranked fifteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Xuan, registered in a military household in Changyuan County, Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuyong; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Lu; his grandfather, Keming; and his father, Shizuo, a prefectural judge. His mother, née Zhang, held the conferred title Lady of Peace. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xi, a prefect; Qi, an honorary official for public benefactions; and Yu, a Gentleman for Rendering Service. His younger brother was Lian, an assistant instructor. He married a woman née Song. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Jian, registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Changben; he was second in birth order, aged forty-nine, and born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zishao; his grandfather, Li, a prefectural school instructor; and his father, Yu. His mother was née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yan. He married a woman née Xie. He placed fifty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Keshou, registered in a civilian household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shouzheng; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yanhe; his grandfather, Mengzhang; and his father, Wenmin. His mother was née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Keheng. He married a woman née Lin. He placed eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Lian, registered in a civilian household in Jiyang County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Ruqi; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Sili; and his father, Ming. His mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Rui and Zhen. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Ding, registered in an official household of the Front Battalion of Fuzhou Central Guard, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Qizhi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang (Vice Battalion Commander), his grandfather was Zhi, his father was Zuo (Instructor), and his mother was née Gao; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zi and Bian, and his wife was née Li. He placed fiftieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Hongyi, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shicuo, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziying, his grandfather was Xiongying (posthumously appointed Secretary), his father was Bi (Prefect), and his mother was née Wang (honored with the title Lady of Peace); both parents were living. His elder brother was Hongzheng; his younger brothers were Hongli, Hongzuo, Hongxuan, Hongzhi, Hongyong, Honggui, and Hongyu; and his wife was née Ling. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Jun, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongshen, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jizong, his grandfather was Dachu, his father was Zhu, and his mother was née Gong; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ze and Lian; his younger brothers were Song, Hong, and Cheng; and his wife was née Fei. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Wei, registered in a military household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhongduan, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benchu, his grandfather was Shining, his father was Ying, and his mother was née He; his father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Tong, his younger brothers were Jin and Zong, and his wife was née He. He placed twenty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

鄧應仁，貫廣東廣州府南海縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子榮，行一，年三十八，五月初五日生。曾祖天澤，祖彦芳，父璲，母劉氏，繼母胡氏。慈侍下，弟應義、應謙、應奎、應璧，娶潘氏。廣東鄉試第一名，會試第二百二名。

李芳，貫四川叙州府宜賓縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字資元，行二，年四十三，正月二十九日生。曾祖廣〔所大使〕，祖貴，父致和，母殷氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，兄蕃，弟芝、蘭、華，娶栗氏。四川鄉試第六十一名，會試第二百五十八名。

張濬，貫山西太原府代州，軍籍，州學生，治書經，字宗舜，行一，年三十一，四月初五日生。曾祖文質，祖銘，父子讓，母徐氏。具慶下，娶吴氏。山西鄉試第四十二名，會試第二百二十九名。
translation_en:
Xiao Chong, registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Linghan. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-three [?] and was born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuexian; his grandfather, Ruming; and his father, Shao〔commissioner of a Tax Office〕. His mother was née Yu 喻. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Ying, and his younger brothers were Teng, Fang, Zhang, Yu, and Rong. His wife was née Yu 余. He placed sixty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Yingren, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zirong. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tianze; his grandfather, Yanfang; and his father, Sui. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Hu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Yingyi, Yingqian, Yingkui, and Yingbi. His wife was née Pan. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Fang, registered in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziyuan. Second in birth order, he was aged forty-three and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guang〔commissioner of an unspecified office〕; his grandfather, Gui; and his father, Zhihe. His mother was née Yin, and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fan, and his younger brothers were Zhi, Lan, and Hua. His wife was née Li 栗. He placed sixty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jun, registered in Daizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zongshun. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhi; his grandfather, Ming; and his father, Zirang. His mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wu. He placed forty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

呂卣〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣，匠籍，府學生，治書經，字宜中，行二，年三十六，正月初三日生〕。曾祖福，祖敬之，父誠，母王氏，繼母郭氏。具慶下，兄彝，娶惠氏。應天府鄉試第六名，會試第二百七十七名。

translation_en:
Zou Xiang 鄒祥 was registered in Dezhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanji; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-one sui, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongde, his grandfather Mingyuan, and his father Bin; his mother was née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Feng, and his younger brothers were Cheng and Xian. His wife was née Liang. He placed nineteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Tingxuan 樊廷選 was registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shunju; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two sui, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guangrong, his grandfather Wen, and his father Zongli; his mother was née Zheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Chen. He placed seventy-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü You 呂卣 was registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in an artisan household, and was a prefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yizhong; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-six sui, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Jingzhi, and his father Cheng; his mother was née Wang, and his stepmother née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yi, and his wife was née Hui. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ju 劉聚 was registered in Yongshou County, Qianzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Benren; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three sui, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong (posthumously granted the title of Secretary), his grandfather Jie (Prefect), and his father Ning; his mother and stepmother were both née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Hui, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Jingzhi, his grandfather Youzhong, and his father Yongqing; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Lai, and both parents were living; his elder brothers were Yuanying, Yuanyang, and Jun (an Assistant Instructor), his younger brothers Yuanfu and Yuanfeng, and his wife was née Qiu; he placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Lun 楊綸, courtesy name Lizhi, was registered in Danyang County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in an artisan household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouqian, his grandfather Jingrong, his father Wensheng, and his mother née Sun, with both parents living; his younger brothers were Gang and Ji, his wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife née Da; he placed seventy-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ning Xian 甯賢, courtesy name Guozheng, was registered in Dingbian Guard in the directly administered region, in a military household, and was a native of Jishan County, Shanxi; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Shi, his adoptive father Gang, and his mother née Liu, with both parents living; his wife was née Zhu; he placed eighty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhi 張智, courtesy name Shouyu, was registered in Julu County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a commoner household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, fourth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bochuan, his grandfather Kuan, his father Qin (a Clerk in a Salt Distribution Commission), and his mother née Wang, with both parents living; his elder brothers were Zhong (an honorary official for public benefaction), Ming, and Li, his younger brothers Ren and Yi, and his wife was née Yin; he placed eighty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張烜〔貫福建福州府福清縣，鹽籍，儒士，治詩經，字伯彰，行一，年三十四，八月三十日生〕。曾祖子仁，祖源，父文第，母王氏。嚴侍下，弟燠，娶林氏。福建鄉試第十名，會試第二百六十四名。
translation_en:
Zhang Feng, courtesy name Yingshi, was registered in a military household in Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guike; his grandfather, Shen; his father, Wei; his mother, née Zhou; and his stepmother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His wife was née Xia. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yan, courtesy name Shoufu, was registered in a military household in Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guiwu; his grandfather, Liangqing; his father, Neng; and his mother, née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ting and Jian, and his wife was née Shen. He ranked seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Yu, courtesy name Chengzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the third day of the intercalary eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junli; his grandfather, Bohou; his father, Shunxi; and his mother, née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yong, his younger brother was Po, and his wife was née Qian. He ranked thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xuan, courtesy name Bozhang, was registered in a salt-producing household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A Confucian scholar, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the thirtieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziren; his grandfather, Yuan; his father, Wendi; and his mother, née Wang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Yu, and his wife was née Lin. He ranked tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Lian, registered in Lingbao County, Shanzhou, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Dechun. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Keming (Left Censor-in-Chief), his grandfather Chun, and his father Mao (an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions); his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jian, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Bi, registered in Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingzhi. First in birth order, he was aged forty-four and was born on the twelfth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Shi, his grandfather Shun, and his father Gui; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jinda (a tribute student, gongshi), and his wife was née Yin. He placed ninth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ji, registered in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yongqi. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-five and was born on the seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Minzhong, his grandfather Mao, and his father Jian; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yu, and he was betrothed to a woman née Wang. He placed second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qi, registered with the Wugong Central Guard in a military household, was originally from Yizhen County in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yunji. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the thirtieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Shu, and his father Yi; his mother was née Ma. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Fu and You, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Hou, courtesy name Hongzai, was registered in a civilian household in Ren County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather, Su, was a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Ren, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yanhong and Yanying, and his wife was née Hao. He placed eighty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tai, courtesy name Daoheng, was registered in a military household in Yicheng County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenbiao; his grandfather, Bingxin, and father, Fuzheng, both held the honorary title of Charitable Official (yiguan); his mother was née Li. Both parents were living, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Xuan, courtesy name Ruqi, was registered in a civilian household in Chongqing Subprefecture, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenda; his grandfather was Zhong; his father was Benchu, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Lu, his younger brother was Shan, and his wife was née Xu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Lü, courtesy name Yonghe, was registered in a civilian household in Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongzhen; his grandfather was Shining; his father was Chongtan [?], and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhi and Wei, and his wife was née Sheng. He placed seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fu Shu 傅㴻, courtesy name Yuehui, was a National University student from a civilian household registered in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, specializing in the Book of Odes; third in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanxian; his grandfather, Ruqi; his father, Bangben, posthumously appointed Examining Editor; and his mother, née Jian, posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Han, Senior Compiler concurrently serving as Proofreader, and Chun; his younger brothers were Shi, Pu, Xun, and Zi; his wife was née Qian. He placed sixty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhuan 汪僎, courtesy name Jianzhi, was a National University student from a civilian household registered in Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, specializing in the Book of Documents; first in birth order, he was aged twenty-two and born on the third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhifu, an Instructor; his grandfather, Zhongduan; his father, Feng, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother, née Zhu; he had living parents and grandparents. His younger brothers were You, Jun, Wei, and Dian; his wife was née Xu. He placed fifty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Hua 黃華, courtesy name Shifu, was a National University student from a civilian household registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, specializing in the Book of Documents; second in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and born on the first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shiheng; his grandfather, Yanzhen; his father, Zhongshu; and his mother, née Xu; both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenji, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Rong Hua 榮華, courtesy name Gongshi, was a county school student from a military household registered in Lantian County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, specializing in the Book of Odes; first in birth order, he was aged twenty-seven and born on the seventeenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather, He; his father, Qing, a County Registrar; and his mother, née Wang; both parents were living. His younger brother was Fu, and his wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

韓春〔貫直隸保定府蠡縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字時元，行一，年三十七，九月初九日生〕。曾祖繼祖，祖玉，父林，嫡母丘氏，生母張氏。慈侍下，弟景暘、景和，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第七十七名，會試第二百五十四名。

translation_en:
Chang Xin, registered in a military household in Xiangcheng County, Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shimian; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ruixing; his grandfather, Zhongmei, was posthumously awarded the title of Supervising Secretary; his father, Ning, was Vice Minister of the Court of Horse Pasturage; and his mother, née Geng, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Qing and Pan, and he married a woman née Shang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Huai, registered in a civilian household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yingzhen; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boda, his grandfather Yi, and his father Ying; his mother was née Feng and his stepmother née Lu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Huaizhen and Huaiyu, and he married a woman née Guo. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Chun, registered in a civilian household in Li County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shiyuan; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jizu, his grandfather Yu, and his father Lin; his father's principal wife was née Qiu, and his birth mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Jingyang and Jinghe, and he married a woman née Li. He placed seventy-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Kan, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shunqing; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Hong, was a Subprefectural Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Qianfu; his father, Mishi, was an honorary official; and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yin, Pei, Zai, Shu, Shan, and Lu, and he married a woman née Zhu. He placed sixty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Mi, registered in an official household of the Qunmu Office (Herds Office) in Shanxi and a native of Chuzhou in Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jingzhi; he was third in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zaifu was posthumously granted the title of Vice Battalion Commander; his grandfather Quan and father Li both held that office. His father’s former wife was Lady Huang, and his mother was Lady Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Guang, a Vice Battalion Commander, and Ding. He married Lady Zhang. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Luan, registered in a civilian household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yingxiang; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingde, his grandfather Weiyi, and his father Yuxin. His father’s former wife was Lady Li, his mother was Lady Zhao, and his stepmother was Lady Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Tai, Zhen, and Feng; his younger brother was Qian. He married Lady Xu. He placed fifteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zi, registered in a military household in Gucheng County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Rubi; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Xianqing, and his father Rong. His mother was Lady Zhu, and his stepmother was Lady Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yun and Zhen. He married Lady Wu. He placed nineteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Liangyu, registered in a military household of the Chengdu Central Guard in Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Dechun; he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Caifu, his grandfather Jingyuan, and his father Xuan. His mother and stepmother were both surnamed Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Liangjin; his younger brothers were Liangzhao, Lianghan, Liangcai, Liangru, and Liangchen. He married Lady Zheng and subsequently Lady Xu. He placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Shiqi and was fifth in birth order, aged forty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather, Jichuan; and his father, An, a County Vice Magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Yan, his stepmother née Zheng, and his birth mother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jun, Jie, Yan, and Lun. He married a woman née He. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Gong 梁鞏 was registered in a civilian household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Bangning and was second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanzheng; his grandfather, Mengcai; his father, Ji; and his mother, née Mai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yu and his younger brother Ji. He married a woman née Ye. He placed thirty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yiyan 王一言 was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Xingzhi and was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shaozong; his grandfather, Zuo; his father, Shouyue, a county school Instructor; and his mother, née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yixin, Yi'e, Yizhi, a student of the National University, and Yiwei; his younger brothers were Yijian and Yihe. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang An 張安 was registered in a military household in Huan County, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Wenjing and was fourth in birth order, aged forty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wentong; his grandfather, Hezhi; and his father, Li, an Investigating Censor. His father's principal wife was née Wang and his birth mother née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wen, Hao, and Pu. He married a woman née Ding and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Fan, registered in a civilian household in Nanxi County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Tingyong, he was third in birth order, and he was forty years old, born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi Yuanding [?], his grandfather Wensu, and his father Luan; his mother was née He and his stepmother née Yin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zigao and Ziben, and his younger brother Ziyu; his wife was née Wu. He ranked eighteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Xun, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jinghui, he was sixth in birth order, and he was twenty-six years old, born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhishan, his grandfather Mengqi, and his father Bin; his father's principal wife was née Pan and his birth mother née Fang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Bing, Huan, Yan, Xu, and Liao; he was betrothed to a woman née Sun. He ranked nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Tang, registered in a civilian household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingyu, he was sixth in birth order, and he was thirty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yang, his grandfather Xinren, and his father Xiu; his father's former wife was née Ding and his mother née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xu (a metropolitan graduate, jinshi), Cheng, Wei, Zhen (a tribute scholar, gongshi), and Yang; his younger brother was Hu, and his wife was née Zheng. He ranked eighty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Feng, registered in a military household in Xincai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Mingqi, he was first in birth order, and he was twenty-five years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gong, his grandfather Ying, and his father Duan; his mother was née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Huang, Lan, and Pei; his wife was née Liu. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Dewei; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jishan, his grandfather Shixiang, his father Wang 瀇, and his mother née Wang 汪. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Fei, Gai, and Gan, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed sixtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mei Chun, registered in an officer household of the Nanjing capital guards and originally from Xiayi County, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yizhi; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Shunchang was Vice Commissioner-in-Chief; his grandfather Yin and father Sheng were both Commanders. His mother, née Liu, had been conferred the title of Lady of the Third Rank (shuren). His father was deceased and his mother living. He was betrothed to a woman née Zhang. He placed ninety-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Lu, registered in a civilian household in Boluo County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruxue; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenqing, his grandfather Huikang, and his father Bing. His father's former wife was née Yang, his mother née Xiao, and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fu, his younger brother Qi, and his wife née Li. He placed seventy-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ning, registered in a civilian household in Wuwei Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanxun; he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziyu, his grandfather Yansheng, and his father Tai, Gentleman for Rendering Service. His mother was née Guo and his stepmother née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yigong, Yishun, Yijing, and Yiqing, and his wife was née Xu. He placed twenty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Shi, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Liangyong, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kan; his grandfather, Zhuan; his father, Hao; and his mother, née Liang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ge, Ti, Guang, Yu, Kai, and Ji, and his wife was née Wang. He placed ninety-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yingxi, registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuwen, and he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongjing; his grandfather, Dingqing; his father, Qianji; and his mother, née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Lin, Yingzhi, Qi, a Case Reviewer, and Yingzhen, and his wife was née Xiao. He placed sixty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Han, registered in Qinshui County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shuyuan, and he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, a District Magistrate; his grandfather, Xun; his father, Cong, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Tan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Hao and Ze; his younger brothers were Pu, Ying, and Yue; and his wife was née Zhang. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳裕〔貫武功中衛軍籍，浙江餘姚縣人，國子生，治禮記，字天弘，行一，年三十五，十一月二十日生〕。曾祖漢英，祖敏成，父文海，前母翁氏，母陳氏，繼母潘氏、瞿氏。重慶下，弟祥、祚，娶韓氏。順天府鄉試第五名，會試第一百六名。

translation_en:
Jiang Xuekui, of civilian registration in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yichen; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather was Wei, Director of a School of Yin-yang Studies; his father was Wei 渭; and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Gao and his younger brother Long; his wife was née Shen. He placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Jue, of artisan registration in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenyu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zitai, his grandfather Long, his father Chao, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing, an Assistant Instructor; his younger brothers were Zan, Ying, Xuan, Zhang, and Ji. His wife was née Lin. He placed sixty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yu, of military registration in Wugong Central Guard and a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Tianhong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hanying, his grandfather Mincheng, and his father Wenhai. His father's former wife was née Weng, his mother was née Chen, and his stepmothers were née Pan and née Qu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Xiang and Zuo; his wife was née Han. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Gong, of civilian registration in Yongxing County, Chenzhou Subprefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Dewen; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Demin, a Judge; his grandfather was Yong, a Prefectural Investigator; his father was Yue, a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Tian, an Instructor in a School of Yin-yang Studies, and his younger brother was Yu; his wife was née Cao. He placed fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Weian, posthumously granted the title of Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather was Shuo, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; his father was Xu, his mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Yang; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Sheng (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Jian, and Ce, his younger brother was Zhen, and his wife was née Chen; he placed fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Xian, registered in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wenhui, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged forty-three, born on the third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tianlu, his grandfather was Rong, his father was Sishun, and his mother was née Huangfu; his mother alone was living, his elder brothers were Tong and Di, and his wife was née Zhang; he placed sixty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ji, registered in Gaocheng County, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xuxu, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju, his grandfather was Cong, a County Vice Magistrate, his father was Qing, and his mother was née Jia; his mother alone was living, and his wife was née Hou; he placed ninety-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Han, registered in Kai County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenyuan, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengcong, his grandfather was Zhicheng, his father was Zhong, and his mother was née Fang; both parents were living, his elder brother was Zichang, his younger brothers were Ziliang and Zigang, and his wife was née Gong; he placed sixty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He placed forty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Yongqing, registered in Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Duanben, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sixing, his grandfather Youcai, and his father Gang; his mother was née Peng, and his stepmother née Hu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Yongji and Yongyuan, and his wife was née Hua. He placed sixteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xun, registered in Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Deguang, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zihe, his grandfather Gongwang, and his father Can, an Instructor; his father's former wife was née Xiao, and his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Yao, his younger brothers were Hua, Kui, and Yi, and his wife was née Zhou. He placed sixtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Quan, registered in an official household of Yongzhou Guard, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Bingheng; he was the eldest son, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Chaojun, grandfather Jing, and father Qi each served as a Guard Pacification Officer. His mother, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father was still living, and his mother was deceased. His younger brothers were Zhi, Yue, Xiang, Luan (a metropolitan graduate), Jin, Xi, Gao, and Yin. He married a woman née Tang. He ranked fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Xiang, registered in a civilian household in Guishan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yinglong; he was the eldest son, aged twenty-three, and born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather Hu, and his father Xin, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His mother was née Liang. His parents and grandparents were still living. His younger brothers were Xi, Tao, Li, and Zhi. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked twelfth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Yongsheng, registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional student of the county school who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shunju; he was the eldest son, aged thirty-four, and born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Bocheng, his grandfather Yanqi, and his father Mengbing. His legal mother was née Zhou, and his birth mother was née Liu. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His younger brother was Yongbian. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked forty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Zongde was registered in a “female household” [?] of the Nanjing Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture. He was a Confucian scholar who specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tianshen; he was the eldest son, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xiufu, his grandfather Lin, and his father Guang. His mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ang and Mian. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He ranked ninety-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.
